messages:
Maya: Quick sync on long-term platform routing + launch criteria. We need a concise playbook for tenant isolation lanes that product, infra, and CS can commit to. Anyone have major blockers?

Devon: Thinking we should ship a two-stage approach: 1) isolation-by-policy (soft lane, no hardware split) to validate semantics; 2) physical isolation for high-SLA customers. Minimizes infra churn early.

Priya: From Platform POV: soft lane is doable but we need precise eviction semantics and a deterministic cost model for shared pools. Without that, downstream teams will see unpredictable token costs.

Logan: Ops notes: telemetry must include per-tenant token burn and KV cache hit rates. Also need an automated throttle circuit that trips before noisy tenants impact p99.

Anna: CS perspective: customers expect migration playbooks and a clear rollback window. Also ask for recommended blackout windows per region to avoid business hours impact.

Maya: Draft launch criteria proposal: (A) telemetry & tracing for isolation lanes in staging + prod; (B) canary with two pilot customers for 21-28 days; (C) rollback/runbook documented; (D) pricing bands mapped to SLA tiers. Agree?

Devon: Additions: - Entitlement table mapping (free/shared/reserved/dedicated) to routing behavior. - A staging traffic-replay test that can emulate 10x peak to validate fallback.

Priya: SLOs we care about for launch: p95 latency delta <= 20% vs baseline, p99 delta <= 40%, KV-cache hit rate >= 90% for cached workloads, eviction events <= 0.3% per hour.

Logan: For canary we should reserve 15% of a node pool for safety so fallback is predictable. Also will create a synthetic tenant that intentionally causes cache thrash to validate isolation.

Maya: Sketch routing policy (informal):
```yaml
routing_policy:
  name: isolation-lane-alpha
  tiers:
    - name: shared
      route: best_effort
      eviction_policy: soft_trim
    - name: reserved
      route: quota_isolation
      eviction_policy: aggressive_trim
    - name: dedicated
      route: hard_split
      eviction_policy: manual_evict
  fallback_sequence:
    - variant_compat
    - reduced_context_model
  canary:
    enabled: true
    pilots: [pilot-corp, pilot-platform]
    duration_days: 21
```

Anna: Can we attach a customer-facing checklist? They need: data residency confirmation, expected downtime window, and test prompts for verification.

Devon: I'll own the entitlement matrix and the policy-as-code prototype (ticket: PLAT-721). Priya: can you own SLO drafts and alert rules? Logan: create canary capacity reservation and synthetic test tenants. Anna: gather pilot customer approvals.

Priya: I'll post SLOs + example alert thresholds tomorrow. Also proposing an "eviction-sim" toggle in staging to run scheduled eviction drills.

Logan: Note: deploy-bot scheduled infra maintenance Thu 02:00-03:00 UTC. We'll avoid canary cutovers during that window.

Maya: Outstanding question: contractual rollback SLA for dedicated lanes. Proposal: standard 72h for most customers; 24h for premium if we include 24/7 on-call and a runbook.

Anna: Customers who pay for 24h rollback will expect a runbook and a schedule for rehearsals. We should price that accordingly.

Maya: Cool. Let's reconvene Friday to sign off on the playbook. I'll draft a single-page product launch brief and circulate. Thanks all. :sparkles:
